poem.title: Before the Burial

lines: I set the water by her hands.
She kept a loaf of bread for me.
I told her I would turn away.
Her brother waited by the wall.
I told her how I turned away.
She kept a place beside her table.
Their branches rested on my knees.
I heard the names beneath them.

memories.text: World: Vale lays the signed return list before Dione and chooses the earlier basket stanza from the song. Dione reads it, then reads Myrine’s words from Piraeus: “My household’s place was kept, and its basket passed to me.” Dione says, “A waiting basket has reached a person’s hands.”

World: Dione names the later accounts beyond Piraeus: the Sicilian crew, the birds’ refuge, shared peace, the chained gift and the poets below. She asks Vale to return with the actual people, supplies and words each journey has earned.
